name: McKay's Furniture
old_description: Transform Your Home with Stylish Living, Dining, and Office Pieces
about:
McKay's Furniture has operated from North Kingstown, Rhode Island since its founding in 1900 by Kenneth I. McKay. The family-owned retailer began as a local furniture store and has remained under family stewardship for over a century, building a reputation for selling durable, long-lasting pieces.

The company stocks a broad range of indoor and outdoor furniture, including dining sets, sectionals, recliners, bookcases, and marine-grade aluminum and wicker collections for exterior spaces. In addition to retail sales, McKay's provides premium white-glove delivery that includes in-home assembly, placement, and cleanup, as well as design consulting services for residential and commercial clients. The showroom carries collections such as Brantley, Leeward, Sag Harbor, and Hadley Teak, with many items available for immediate pickup.

McKay's serves homeowners, interior designers, and small-business owners furnishing home offices and lounge areas. Interior designers are noted as a key customer segment, drawn by the large in-stock selection and the convenience of the white-glove installation service. The retailer also supports local institutions, partnering with organizations ranging from the Special Olympics and Rhode Island State Police to schools, wildlife refuges, and healthcare charities.

The company emphasizes that its responsibility extends beyond the sale, citing the "final mile" delivery experience as a core differentiator. Its community-focused mission and multi-generational craftsmanship legacy are presented as the foundation of its enduring customer relationships.

name: McKenna Metal
old_description: We embrace challenges and adapt to timelines, budgets, and project revisions better than any shop in the industry. Our staff is equipped with decades of experience in metal fabrication.
about:
McKenna Metal, founded in 1995, operates a 30,000-square-foot facility in the industrial northwest of Portland, Oregon. The company has been locally owned since its inception, though the founder’s name is not publicly disclosed. It began as a metal fabrication shop serving the Portland metro area and has grown to a staff of over 40.

The shop provides sheet metal and rotary tube laser cutting, waterjet cutting, custom welding (TIG, MIG, arc), metal forming via 240-ton and 55-ton press brakes, and powder coating in a 9'x11'x20' booth. Equipment includes an Amada Gemini CNC laser with a 60”x120” shuttle table and an Amada rotary index laser for tube profiles up to 8.66” round. The facility handles materials from mild steel and aluminum to stainless steel, wood, acrylics, and stone, accepting CAD files in AutoCAD and SolidWorks. Production capacity ranges from prototypes to large runs.

McKenna Metal serves businesses and organizations across the Pacific Northwest, with listed service areas including Portland, Tualatin, Beaverton, Hillsboro, and Vancouver, Washington, plus national shipping. Its project portfolio spans architectural metalwork, industrial fabrication, and decorative metal goods sold through its online store, such as garden labels, metal roses, and weldable dice kits.

The company emphasizes quick turnarounds and the ability to adapt to shifting timelines, budgets, and design revisions, positioning itself as a responsive partner for custom metal projects.

name: Mecury Commercial Electronics
old_description: Our Advanced Concepts Group brings experts in early, so we know what’s possible and what isn’t, before missions even ask.
about:
Headquartered in Hudson, New Hampshire, Mercury Systems (operating under the Mecury Commercial Electronics name) designs and manufactures advanced electronics for aerospace and defense missions. The company operates a 50,000-square-foot production facility on its Phoenix campus, which opened recently to expand capacity and accelerate delivery timelines.

Its product portfolio includes direct RF multi-chip modules such as the RFS1140 built on AMD Versal adaptive SoCs, rad-tolerant 6U SpaceVPX processing boards like the SCFE6933, small-form-factor RF subsystems such as the DRF4580L with Intel Agilex 9 FPGAs, and broadband MMIC components for rugged defense environments. The company emphasizes chip-scale integration, open architectures, and model-based systems engineering to move from concept to production quickly.

Mercury serves the aerospace, defense, and space sectors, including missile defense, electronic warfare, and satellite programs. It has supported more than 75 spacecraft across all orbits and claims participation in every Mars mission over the past two decades. Customers include prime contractors and government agencies requiring ITAR-compliant, MIL-STD-qualified hardware for land, sea, air, and space domains.

The firm's Advanced Concepts Group engages early in technology development to shape commercial innovations into operational advantages, a strategy the company says ensures its solutions remain ahead of evolving threat environments.

name: Med Tech Sweden
old_description: Throughout all these years, since 1968, Bo has worked continually; while also developing and testing products to stabilize fractures until they may be examined in the hospital.
about:
Med Tech Sweden, Inc. is based in Geneseo, Illinois, where it has operated since 2008. The company traces its origins to 1968 when founder Bo Rickard E. Renberg, a Swedish Air Force firefighter-EMT and later a registered nurse and mobile intensive care nurse, began developing fracture-stabilization devices. Renberg’s career spanned four decades in emergency medical services across Sweden, including leadership roles in the Swedish Rescue and Emergency Medicine Association and the Nordic Ambulance Cooperation Group.

The firm manufactures patented emergency first-responder equipment designed by Renberg in Sweden and produced in its Geneseo shop from U.S.-sourced materials. Each unit undergoes individual rigorous testing before release. Product lines focus on lightweight, environmentally friendly solutions for fracture stabilization and rescue situations where no satisfactory options previously existed.

Customers include U.S. Olympic teams, professional sports organizations such as the Denver Broncos, Dallas Cowboys, and Dallas Mavericks, major healthcare institutions like UCLA, Vanderbilt, Purdue, Sweden’s Queen Silvia Hospital for Children, and Baltimore’s Children’s Hospital, as well as fire departments (Tampa, FDNY EMS), military branches (U.S. Air Force, Homeland Security), ski patrols (Aspen, Vail, Steamboat Springs), motorsports (FIA European Racing), and humanitarian groups (Red Cross of Iceland and Italy, Swedish Coast Guard).

The company emphasizes that its equipment is the most lightweight, environmentally friendly, and medically safe in its class, a claim rooted in Renberg’s frontline experience and continuous product refinement since 1968.

name: Med-Dyne
old_description: As the leading provider of EEG, ECG, and Apnea Monitoring Supplies, Med-Dyne is committed to providing exceptional quality in every aspect.  We always aim to exceed our customers expectations.
about:
Med-Dyne, based in Louisville, Kentucky, was founded in 1996. The company has operated for over three decades as a supplier of medical monitoring supplies.

The company manufactures a range of disposable and reusable electrodes for pediatric ECG monitoring, adult and pediatric sleep testing, infant apnea monitoring, and EEG technology. Its capabilities include custom product design, custom packaging combinations of electrodes in various colors, lengths, and qualities, and the application of a patented hydrogel adhesive designed for sensitive skin. Med-Dyne maintains inventory in stock to avoid backorders and ships orders the same day they are received from its central U.S. location.

Med-Dyne serves healthcare facilities, sleep labs, and pediatric care providers that require cardiac and neurological monitoring supplies. Customers include hospitals and clinics needing pediatric ECG electrodes, sleep testing electrodes, and apnea monitoring sensors. The company also provides expert advice on product use and customizes packaging to facility specifications.

Med-Dyne differentiates itself through its patented hydrogel adhesive that provides a firm yet gentle bond for fragile patients, same-day shipping on all orders including custom-packaged products, and a commitment to maintaining stock so backorders are eliminated. The central U.S. location enables fast delivery nationwide.

name: MedCOR Professionals
old_description: The Medical Suppliers with the Most Personalized Service in Maine
about:
MedCOR Professionals operates a medical supply store in Scarborough, Maine, where it has served patients and clinics since its founding in 1995. The business began as a local supplier focused on providing personalized care across all phases of health and recovery, and it remains one of the few companies in New England covering that full continuum.

The company does not manufacture products but works directly with vendors to source and distribute a range of home medical supplies, bracing and support products, and pain management solutions. Its services include filing Medicare and insurance claims, managing vendor communications, handling billing, tracking, and returns, and scheduling routine product deliveries for clinics. The Scarborough location functions as a retail and distribution point, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

MedCOR Professionals serves home-care patients, medical clinics, and healthcare providers throughout Maine. Concrete examples from its offerings include post-operative bras for breast surgery recovery, walking boots, and multi-post therapy collars. The company also supplies clinics with scheduled deliveries of equipment and consumables, positioning itself as a single-source partner for both individual patients and institutional customers.

The firm emphasizes personalized, compassionate service as its differentiator, highlighting its ACHC accreditation as evidence of compliance with national quality standards. Its stated mission is to enhance patient care through quality clinic supplies and to provide an exceptional patient experience by handling administrative burdens such as insurance claims and vendor coordination.

name: Medical Device Academy, Inc.
old_description: Are you a start-up device company that needs medical device consulting services and training for an FDA 510k submission?
about:
Medical Device Academy, Inc. operates from Shrewsbury, Vermont, with a fully remote team of ten consultants spread across the Eastern Time Zone, including North Carolina, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Vermont. The founding year is not publicly disclosed, nor is the ownership structure. The firm's principal, Rob Packard, brings over 30 years of medical device, pharmaceutical, and biotechnology experience, including a stint as CEO and co-founder of a laparoscopic imaging start-up in 2004.

The company functions as a quality and regulatory consulting firm specializing in FDA 510(k) submissions using the eSTAR template, FDA pre-submissions via PreSTAR, quality system implementation for FDA, ISO 13485, and MDSAP compliance, and internal quality system audits. It also provides FDA U.S. Agent services, CE Marking technical file preparation, Canadian medical device license applications, and a curated suite of training products—including a 510(k) course series, procedure templates, and on-demand webinars. All work is performed virtually; the firm does not manufacture physical products.

Clients are primarily small and mid-size medical device companies, start-ups with proof-of-concept prototypes, and non-U.S. firms seeking FDA market entry. The academy also serves companies needing continuing education, quality system auditing, and regulatory pathway analysis for U.S., European, and Canadian markets. Engagements often begin at the early prototype stage and extend through submission and post-market compliance.

The firm differentiates itself with flat-fee pricing—enabled by a narrow focus on 510(k) and De Novo pathways—and a team that has designed and built medical devices, not just advised on them. Packard's background as a former Notified Body lead auditor (2009–2012) and start-up CEO informs a practical, teaching-oriented approach aimed at helping clients avoid costly testing repeats and remediation.
